me.title: Methodology & Data Quality
me.intro: SkillSense combines four heterogeneous signals into one Demand Index per district-trade-month, calibrates it to annual openings, forecasts 12 months ahead with prediction intervals, and compares it with expected employable supply from training seats.
items: All data is SIMULATED. Real government feeds are represented by documented connector interfaces.
Demand Index = Σ weight × robust z-score of each source; weights are re-normalised over available sources and reduced for sparse data.
Annual openings are calibrated from a PLFS-style employment baseline × turnover rate; turnover rates are assumptions.
Supply = seats × enrolment × completion × placement-ready share + carry-over of unplaced certified candidates (retention assumed 50%).
Forecast intervals are calibrated on earlier backtest origins; coverage on holdout origins is reported honestly and may differ on real data.
District forecasts are reconciled top-down to the state-trade forecast so levels add up; MinT reconciliation is a documented extension.
Mapping accuracy is measured on synthetic titles; real postings will be messier. Low-confidence titles go to the review queue.
Severity and flag thresholds are policy parameters and should be set by planners.
formulas: Openings = Baseline × (1 + Σ w̃ · z · spread)
